lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: We can't take it anymore, Pluto. This dog Menippus, living next door to us — either move him somewhere else or we're relocating.
lines.description: outraged tenant complaint, grand but petty

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: What exactly is he doing to you? He's just as dead as you are.

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: Whenever we're mourning and lamenting — Midas here, weeping for his gold; Sardanapalus, for all his luxury; myself, for my treasuries — he laughs at us. He calls us slaves. He calls us filth. And sometimes he starts singing over our laments, just to make it worse. The man is insufferable.
lines.description: sincere grievance, building into scandalized outrage

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Menippus. What do you have to say for yourself.
lines.description: flat judicial summons, tired not angry

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: All true. I despise them — they're worthless and they're pathetic. It wasn't enough that they lived badly; now they're dead and they're still clinging to the world above. [pause] So yes, I take pleasure in annoying them.
lines.description: cheerfully candid, dry delight in confession

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Even so — you shouldn't. They're grieving real losses.
lines.description: mild rebuke, procedural fairness with sympathy

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And you're being foolish, Pluto, if you're siding with their moaning.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: I'm not siding with anyone. I just don't want conflict in my jurisdiction.
lines.description: exasperated building manager, practical not moral

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well then, you absolute dregs of Lydia, Phrygia, and Assyria — let me be very clear: I am not stopping. Wherever you go, I will follow. I will annoy you. I will sing over you. I will laugh at you.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No. What you did — that was an outrage. Demanding to be worshipped. Lording it over free men. Never once giving death a single thought. So go ahead and wail. Everything you had has been taken away.
lines.description: calm verdict, amused but morally sharp

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: So much. [sighs] So much, and all of it great.

lines.speaker: Sardanapalus
lines.description: effete, theatrical little sob of luxury lost

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Excellent. Keep going — you mourn, and I'll sing you a round of 'Know thyself' as the refrain. [pause] Seems fitting, really, for that kind of wailing.
lines.description: delighted deadpan, punchline lands without mugging
